subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance - post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Diana Mercer <diana.mercer@healthcorp.com>, Rajiv Banerjee <rajiv@medsys.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance - post-call recap

Hi Diana / Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the MAP milestone focused on Data Handling & Compliance: retention, logging/audit trails, and PHI/PII constraints.

Key takeaways from today's discovery:
- HealthCorp will be sending patient-identifiable inference requests (PHI scope) for a subset of workflows; the rest are general product/text.
- Legal requires retention window <= 90 days for raw request content, with longer indexed metadata retention for auditing.
- Need proof points for: SOC 2 controls, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, and detailed audit logging (who/what/when token-level traces).

Proposed MAP milestone (draft attached: Redwood_MAP_DataHandling_v1.xlsx):
1) Define retention policy & retention-by-data-type (owner: HealthCorp Legal / Redwood AE) — target complete: 2026-08-20
2) Logging & audit trails scope (owner: HealthCorp Infra / Redwood SRE) — target complete: 2026-08-16
3) PHI/PII processing constraints (owner: HealthCorp Legal + Redwood Security) — target complete: 2026-08-20
4) KMS/encryption & key management validation (owner: HealthCorp SecOps / Redwood Security) — target complete: 2026-08-18

Dependencies:
- Final list of endpoints that will carry PHI (HealthCorp devs)
- Legal review of sample retention policy language (HealthCorp Legal)
- Access to a short test dataset or representative payload (sanitized) for logging proof-of-concept

Next steps I propose:
- HealthCorp to confirm owners for each bullet above and surface any missing compliance constraints by EOD 2026-08-05
- Redwood to provide SOC 2 scoped controls and a short one-page tech note on logging granularity by 2026-08-03 (attached)
- Quick 30-min follow-up call next week to lock the target close date for the MAP milestone(s) if we have owners confirmed

Attaching: Redwood_MAP_DataHandling_v1.xlsx (MAP draft).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into the MAP.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Diana Mercer <diana.mercer@healthcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Banerjee <rajiv@medsys.io>, Legal Ops <legal@healthcorp.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - post-call recap

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the MAP draft. A few quick clarifications from our side: we do expect PHI in two endpoints (patient intake and claim reconciliation). Legal has flagged the 90-day raw retention as a starting point — we may require a shorter window for certain fields (SSN, full DOB). Can you confirm if Redwood supports per-field retention policies or only per-request retention?

Also, our security team needs more detail on the audit logs: specifically, are token-level events (model input/response hashes) retained, and can we get immutable, exportable audit trails for a rolling 12-month period for metadata?

Looping in Legal Ops for visibility.

Best,
Diana Mercer
Head of Product Integrations, HealthCorp
Diana.Mercer@healthcorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Diana Mercer <diana.mercer@healthcorp.com>, Rajiv Banerjee <rajiv@medsys.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - post-call recap

Thanks Diana — great questions. Quick answers and an updated (actionable) milestone breakdown below. I'm attaching our SOC2 scoped controls pdf as well.

Short answers:
- Per-field retention: Redwood supports configurable retention policies at the route/endpoint level today; per-field retention can be implemented via a lightweight pre-ingest transform (we can include this in the MAP workstream and own the implementation cadence).
- Audit logs: We retain token-level metadata (timestamps, route, model version, request/response hashes) and can provide exportable, immutable logs for metadata for up to 12 months. Raw request content retention is configurable per-route and can be limited to 90 days or less.

Updated MAP milestones (owner & dependencies):
A) Retention policy & implementation plan
   - Owner: HealthCorp Legal (define policy) / Redwood (implement route-level retention + optional pre-ingest transform)
   - Target: 2026-08-20
   - Dependencies: list of PHI endpoints; sample sanitized payloads
B) Logging & Audit Trail delivery
   - Owner: HealthCorp Infra (acceptance criteria) / Redwood SRE (deliver exportable audit artifacts)
   - Target: 2026-08-16
   - Acceptance criteria: exportable CSV/JSON with immutable metadata for 12 months; request/response hash present
C) PHI/PII constraints & redaction plan
   - Owner: HealthCorp Legal + Redwood Security
   - Target: 2026-08-20
   - Dependencies: legal sign-off on per-field redaction language
D) KMS & encryption validation
   - Owner: HealthCorp SecOps / Redwood Security
   - Target: 2026-08-18
   - Dependencies: key rotation policy; KMS integration test account
E) Final sign-off & enablement runbook
   - Owner: HealthCorp Ops / Redwood Solutions Eng
   - Target: 2026-08-24

Please review these owners and dates; if HealthCorp can confirm owners for A/B/C by 2026-08-05, Redwood will schedule the SRE/KMS checkpoints and produce a short data handling runbook for your Ops team.

Call to action:
- Diana / Legal Ops: please confirm whether per-field retention is a hard requirement or if the pre-ingest transform approach would be acceptable.
- Rajiv: can your team provide representative sanitized payloads by 2026-08-06?

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for next week; propose 2026-08-06 or 2026-08-09 — let me know which works.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Banerjee <rajiv@medsys.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diana Mercer <diana.mercer@healthcorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - post-call recap

Marissa / Diana —

Thanks for the thorough update. HealthCorp is generally aligned with the milestones and the proposed dates; Legal will run through the per-field vs. pre-ingest approach but are amenable to the transform approach if we get a clear traceability model. One final technical question for Redwood Security: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with our KMS, and can you provide a short checklist for the KMS integration validation?

Assuming that answer is yes, we can accept these milestones pending final Legal review — target close date on our side: 2026-08-24 for the overall MAP milestone group.

Can we book a 30-min tech check on 2026-08-06 at 10:00am PT to go over KMS and the logging export format?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Senior Engineering Manager, MedSys (integrations lead for HealthCorp)
rajiv@medsys.io
